overview: S12 is the server telling the client to apply a velocity vector, normally knockback, and every anticheat treats it as a promise: the client's next movement ticks must reflect the vector it was sent. The corpus splits into direct statistical checks (Azure VelocityA compares the vertical delta against the sent vector) and transaction-ordered simulation checks (Grim KnockbackHandler, Artemis VelocityPreProcessor, Frequency VelocityManager) that know exactly when the packet arrived at the client and require the knockback in the following prediction. This packet is the reason anti-knockback cheats cancel or alter S12 specifically.

checks.name: KnockbackHandler / AntiKB (Grim)
checks.purpose: Requires the client's simulated motion to include the exact knockback vector the server sent, flagging any reduction or delay.
checks.how_it_works: On the OUT side, wraps each entity-velocity packet for the player (or their vehicle) between two transaction packets, recording the vector with the first transaction id. As client transactions arrive, knockbacks move from a future queue into known-taken state; the prediction engine then compares the player's actual movement against the required knockback, accumulating a threshold-bounded buffer and triggering a setback above the immediate threshold.
checks.detects: Anti-knockback, velocity cancel and velocity reduction cheats, including selective cancels that take partial knockback.
checks.variations: Artemis VelocityPreProcessor applies the velocity in a transaction-confirmed pre action; Grim instead leaves it in a queue until the client's transactions prove arrival.

checks.name: VelocityA (Azure)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 statistical check: the reported upward move after a knockback packet must be at least 77 percent of the sent vertical velocity.
checks.how_it_works: Reads the OUT entity-velocity packet, keeps the vertical component (field c divided by 8000.0) when the entity id matches the player, and skips causes that do not produce knockback (starvation, fire, drowning, poison, wither, thorns, fall, lava). On the next upward move it compares deltaY to the recorded velocity and reports the taken percentage as a violation.
checks.detects: Anti-knockback that reduces or zeroes vertical velocity; the percentage reported makes the flag self-documenting.
checks.variations: Rammelkast VelocityCheck and MIU AntiVelocity use the same sent-vector-vs-delta comparison; Grim and Artemis add transaction ordering on top.

checks.name: VelocityManager feed (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Records every player-targeted S12 into a short-lived velocity window that all movement checks read for exemptions and baselines.
checks.how_it_works: The outgoing packet processor wraps each entity-velocity packet, and when the entity id is the player, pushes the vector into the VelocityManager. The manager keeps snapshots with horizontal and vertical magnitudes for two seconds, exposing max values that the speed and invalid checks add to their expected baselines, and the VELOCITY exemption type switches off checks while a recent velocity is active.
checks.detects: Anti-knockback cheats are detected by the speed and invalid checks because the expected velocity baseline is missing or reduced.
checks.variations: Azure VelocityA keeps a single vertical velocity scalar; Frequency keeps a time-windowed deque so exemptions decay naturally.

checks.name: VelocityPreProcessor (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Applies the S12 velocity to the movement holder only after the client confirms the packet, so prediction checks see it in the correct tick.
checks.how_it_works: Matches the OUT entity-velocity packet for the player's entity id, builds a Velocity object, and registers it in the connection's transaction confirmation. The pre action moves the current velocity into lastVelocity and installs the new vector as processed; the post action clears the processed flag when the transaction returns.
checks.detects: Velocity spoofing where a client applies knockback at the wrong time or not at all, which shows up as a prediction residual.
checks.variations: Grim queues knockbacks against transaction ids; Artemis installs them in a confirmation callback, which is the same ordering idea with different storage.
